text.p: Argentine oil company YPF SA on Thursday announced what it described as an "aggressive" plan to expand its business in Argentina and other countries during the next 10 years.

"The fundamental objective for the next 10 years is to grow in all our activities in Argentina and the world at a faster rate than the industry average," said Roberto Monti, executive vice president and general manager of YPF.

"We will look for business opportunities that bring added value to the company, its employees and its shareholders, all this in a very aggressive fashion," he said during a meeting with business leaders and journalists.
With this strategy in mind, the company is redefining its goals for the next six months, he said.

YPF is aiming for annual domestic production growth of six percent overall -- nine percent in natural gas and 3.5 percent in petrol. The forecast for replacing reserves is 120 percent a year in Argentina and 150 percent abroad.
"Gas exports from Argentina are going to grow spectacularly," Monti said.

The executive said YPF is well positioned to expand in Latin America because of strong growth in demand in Brazil and Chile, among other factors. The company already has interests in Bolivia, Ecuador, Indonesia, Peru, the United States and Venezuela.
"The fact we were once a state firm makes negotiations easier with the government oil firms of other countries who are owners of more than 90 percent of world oil reserves," Monti said.

YPF's output is about 600,000 barrels per day of oil and natural gas, or 41 percent of total Argentine output. It accounts for 51 percent of the country's refinery capacity and has 2,415 filling stations, or 44 percent of the total in the country.
